Grid Funding from Data Centers in the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA)

meta.summary:
With the rapid growth in data centers, federal policymakers have been focused on how to make sure that adding large data centers to the electric system does not increase electricity bills for other customers. Recently, a bipartisan group of senators introduced an energy permitting reform bill, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), which […] 
 The post  Grid Funding from Data Centers in the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA)  appeared first on  Grid Strategies .

title: ISO-NE Argues Transitional Cluster Costs Fair, Cites Shrinking Headroom

meta.summary:
ISO-NE defended its cluster study methodology and argued that the high network upgrade cost estimates stemmed from shrinking headroom on its transmission system. 
 The post  ISO-NE Argues Transitional Cluster Costs Fair, Cites Shrinking Headroom  appeared first on  RTO Insider .

title: Analyses Find Senate Permitting Bill Would Benefit Consumers

meta.summary:
The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act would benefit electricity consumers by having data centers pay for upgraded and expanded transmission infrastructure, which in turn would allow for more generation resources to interconnect, according to two analyses. 
 The post  Analyses Find Senate Permitting Bill Would Benefit Consumers  appeared first on  RTO Insider .

title: NYISO Large Load Proposal Passes with ‘State Exempt’ Provision

meta.summary:
The NYISO Management Committee approved proposed tariff revisions intended to satisfy FERC’s Order to Show Cause on large load interconnections after the ISO added a “State Exempt Large Load” category to account for to-be-issued rules by New York state. 
 The post  NYISO Large Load Proposal Passes with ‘State Exempt’ Provision  appeared first on  RTO Insider .

title: Why batteries, not gas plants, should be data centers' first choice

meta.summary: Developers and utilities are building tons of gas generation to power the data center boom.
